About me

I am Syahla Nandina Fayi' Afif, an Automation Engineering Technology Graduate from Universitas Negeri Jakarta, with an interest in automation and construction. I have experience as an Engineering Intern in the Building Automation System (BAS) Division at PT Jaya Teknik Indonesia, where I gained knowledge of HVAC systems and Building Automation Systems. I also have experience as a Civil Engineering Intern at PT Bangunin Bangunan Indonesia, where I was involved in monitoring residential construction progress, drafting floor plans using AutoCAD, creating residential building models using SketchUp, and preparing Bills of Quantity (BoQ) and Cost Estimates.

Proficient in using AutoCAD and SketchUp for drafting and modeling, with basic knowledge of control systems, PLCs, microcontrollers, and Internet of Things (IoT). Committed to continuously developing my technical skills and expanding my professional experience to contribute to various projects and challenges in the industry.

Thesis project: Design and Development of a Smart Cane for Elderly Mobility Using Ultrasonic Sensors and MPU6050 Based on the Mamdani Fuzzy Logic Method

This research presents the design and development of a smart walking stick that supports the mobility of older adults, who commonly suffer from a decline in balance and face a greater risk of falling as they age. The system is built on an ESP32-C3 microcontroller and integrates an HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor to detect obstacles ahead of the user, an MPU6050 sensor to measure the stick's tilt as an indicator of a potential fall, and a Neo-6M GPS module to determine the user's location. Data from the ultrasonic and MPU6050 sensors are processed using Mamdani Fuzzy Logic to assess the user's condition, enabling the system to deliver voice warnings that adapt to the level of risk. Additionally, an emergency (SOS) button allows the user to send an alert message containing their location coordinates via WhatsApp.
